summary: The candidate adds two helper-level geometry tests but no production change. The prepared base already contains plausible replay padding/staging behavior, and independent gfx950 tests found no source-level counterexample. The candidate tests do not exercise graph admission, runner staging, replay metadata refresh, or DSV4 consumption, so they do not establish that the original H20 TP4 illegal-access path is fixed.

tests.what_was_measured: Pre-candidate helper coverage; 10 tests passed, showing the base already had generic padding support.
Candidate helper-level regression suite; 12 tests passed.
Token-tier and request-slot admission boundaries; 2 tests passed on each revision.

Real gfx950 tensor execution through DecodeCudaGraphRunner._stage_ragged_verify_layout for the reported 32x6 case, mixed widths, lower-token tier filling, stable buffer pointers, the native 192-request boundary, and rejection of shrinking 192 rows to 191 slots.

gpu_execution_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 executed the runner staging and ragged tensor kernels under ROCm 7.2; this was not CUDA/H20 graph replay.
remaining_counterexamples: The candidate tests still pass without exercising DecodeCudaGraphRunner._stage_ragged_verify_layout or DSV4 replay metadata, so removal or breakage of that integration is not detected by the proposed regression.
The exact four-H20 TP4 DeepSeek-V4-Flash CUDA Graph replay remains unexecuted and could still expose CUDA/Hopper- or distributed-only failures.
The candidate does not independently cover a lower-token layout rounded to the same 192-token tier, where synthetic padding slots receive tokens rather than remaining zero-length.
remaining_limitations: Only one AMD gfx950 GPU was assigned; the issue reports four NVIDIA H20 GPUs.
The DeepSeek-V4-Flash DSpark model weights were unavailable.
No full serving, CUDA Graph, TP4, or model-semantic reproduction was possible.
No native source changed in the candidate, so rebuilding native code was not applicable.
